questions.prompt: Where do GitHub Actions workflow files live?

options.text: In the repository root as action.yml
In the .github/workflows/ directory as YAML files
In a Docker image
In the registry

questions.explanation: Workflows are YAML files placed in .github/workflows/. Each defines events, jobs, and steps.

questions.prompt: What permission must a job have to push an image to GHCR, and what token does it use?

options.text: contents: write, using a personal SSH key
packages: write, using the automatic GITHUB_TOKEN
No permission is needed
admin: write, using a hard-coded password

questions.explanation: Pushing to GHCR requires permissions: packages: write. The job authenticates with the automatic GITHUB_TOKEN via docker/login-action.

questions.prompt: How do you ensure the image is built and pushed only after tests pass?

options.text: Put both in the same step
Give the build job needs: test so it runs only if the test job succeeds
Run the build job first
Disable tests

questions.explanation: needs: test makes the build-and-push job depend on the test job, so no image is published when tests fail.

questions.prompt: In a workflow, a repository secret named API_KEY is referenced as ${{ ______.API_KEY }}. (one word)
questions.explanation: Secrets are read via ${{ secrets.NAME }}; they must never be hard-coded in the workflow file.

questions.prompt: What does docker/metadata-action do in a build workflow?

options.text: It runs the container
It generates image tags and labels automatically, such as a SHA tag and a semantic-version tag
It scans for vulnerabilities
It deploys to production

questions.explanation: metadata-action computes useful tags and labels (commit SHA, branch, semantic version) that you feed into build-push-action.

questions.prompt: Which are good practices for a container CI/CD workflow? Select all that apply.

options.text: Run tests on every push and pull request
Gate the image build behind passing tests with needs:
Cache builds with cache-from/cache-to type=gha
Hard-code your registry password in the YAML

questions.explanation: Test broadly, gate the build on tests, and cache for speed. Credentials belong in secrets, never hard-coded in the workflow.
